## How to use this guide

You should work through each page step by step.
You should follow along with the examples.
Therefore you will gradually build up a model and your skills as you progress.
there will also be tests at end of pages.

Pre-requisites:

* Installed your chosen programming language
* Installed a suitable IDE to use

## Example models

Alongside the book, four fully implemented example repositories provide complete worked examples that go beyond the in-text code, giving you concrete projects to refer to.

We will mention these at end of page in a section "explore the example models"

## Feedback and citation

If you use and enjoy this guide, we'd love to hear from you! We are excited to hear from people who have used this book. Your feedback and experience can help shape it for future readers and the broader healthcare simulation community.

At the bottom of every page in this book, you'll find a comment section powered by **Giscus**. After signing in with your GitHub account, you can:

* Comment on individual pages to share insights, ask questions, or flag typos/bugs.
* Leave a comment here (or on the home/conclusion pages) to give feedback about the book overall.

**We’d love to hear from you**. If you've used the book, let us know! What worked well? What could be improved? Share any questions, suggestions, success stories, challenges, or ideas for new content.

Prefer email instead? Reach out to the STARS team - you can contact:
